unresolvedQuestions.question: The operative date of Laws 2026, chapter 70, section 5 must be confirmed before participant-facing instructions state it. The session law was retrieved on 2026-08-02: section 5 adds a new paragraph (f) to § 609A.015, subd. 5, under which the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension unseals a record and notifies the judicial branch if it later determines the record did not qualify for automatic relief, making that determination only from a record stored in its criminal history system, and the following paragraphs are renumbered (g) through (j). It does not alter the BCA's identification duty, the court-sealing window or victim notice. Chapter 70 states an effective date only for section 4 (1 January 2027), so section 5 falls to the default in Minn. Stat. § 645.02. Packet identity is unaffected because this route has no packet; the participant-facing warning that a Clean Slate grant may later be unsealed is an instruction change.

controllingAuthority.summary: On written demand, law enforcement and the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension must destroy arrest identification data — fingerprints and thumbprints, photographs, distinctive physical mark identification data, known aliases and street names, and all copies and duplicates — where the person has no felony or gross-misdemeanour conviction anywhere in the ten years immediately preceding determination of all pending criminal actions in their favour, and either all charges were dismissed before a determination of probable cause, or the prosecuting authority declined to file and a grand jury did not indict. Relief is mandatory on demand where the conditions are met. The Minnesota Judicial Branch publishes six sample demand letters.

exclusions: Section 299C.11, subd. 3(1) provides that the following are not a determination in favour of the arrested person: sealing under § 152.18, subd. 1, § 242.31 or chapter 609A; successful completion of a diversion programme; an order of discharge under § 609.165; and a pardon under chapter 638.
Any felony or gross-misdemeanour conviction, in or outside Minnesota, in the ten years immediately preceding determination of all pending criminal actions in the person's favour.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Reclassified from process_guidance to custom_pleading on packet-only re-review. The review itself directs LegalEase to generate a six-agency, participant-signed demand-letter set while classifying the route as guidance because the mechanism is correspondence rather than a pleading. Under the controlling product model a participant-signed demand letter is a packet-generating custom output, and a court filing is not required for custom_pleading. The statute supplies the conditions, the entitlement and the custodians, and the Judicial Branch publishes six official sample letters as drafting references. Relief is mandatory on demand where the conditions are met.

limitations.statement: Use the Minnesota Judicial Branch's six sample letters as authoritative drafting references, not as mandatory fillable forms. The Judicial Branch states they are only examples and must be edited to add case-specific information.

provenance.sourceStatement: The Judicial Branch itself publishes sample letters and states that they "are only examples, and you must edit them and add all of the information specific to your case."

controllingAuthority.summary: Where the prosecutor agrees, the court shall seal without any petition unless it determines that the interests of the public and public safety in keeping the record public outweigh the disadvantages to the subject. The prosecutor's agreement is discretionary and, before agreeing, the prosecutor must make a good-faith effort to notify identifiable victims of the intended agreement and of the opportunity to object. One statewide mechanism with county-specific intake.

exclusions: Dispositions outside the § 609A.02, subd. 3 grounds population.
Pending charges, as under § 609A.02, subd. 3.

waitingPeriods.condition: The § 609A.02, subd. 3 waiting periods apply by reference
waitingPeriods.duration: As under subd. 3. For a person described in subd. 3(a)(2), diversion or stay of adjudication, the prosecutor's agreement may occur before or after the charges are dismissed.

units.label: Request to the prosecuting authority
units.description: The participant asks the prosecuting authority to agree to sealing. LegalEase identifies the correct prosecuting authority from the county and offence location and prepares the participant's factual summary. Which sub-branch applies depends on whether the county runs a published programme.

units.label: County portal application
units.description: Hennepin, Ramsey and Washington Counties run published online applications. These are third-party intake systems with their own field requirements, so LegalEase prepares the participant's factual summary and routes them to the county portal. It does not complete or submit a county portal application.

units.label: Written request to the county or city attorney
units.description: Where the county runs no published programme, the participant contacts the county or city attorney directly. LegalEase generates a participant-signed written request setting out the case, the disposition, the applicable § 609A.02, subd. 3 ground and the participant's own account. The Attorney General page is the statewide entry point for identifying the correct authority.

units.label: Court sealing on prosecutor agreement
units.description: Once the prosecutor agrees, the court shall seal without any participant petition, unless the public-interest balance goes the other way. There is nothing for the participant to file at this stage.

geography.venue: Statewide in authority, county-specific in practice. The county attorney where the county prosecuted; the city attorney where the city prosecuted.

citations: City of St. Paul v. Froysland, 246 N.W.2d 435 (Minn. 1976)
controllingAuthority.summary: A judicially recognised inherent authority to seal judicial branch records, outside chapter 609A. Ambaye sets two grounds: where the petitioner's constitutional rights may be seriously infringed by retention of the records, or, where constitutional rights are not involved, whether expungement yields a benefit to the petitioner commensurate with the disadvantages to the public and the burden on the court. Under Schultz, absent constitutional infringement the judicial branch cannot order non-judicial records sealed, so relief reaches court records only.

exclusions: Police, sheriff, prosecutor and BCA records, which remain public because relief reaches judicial branch records only.
The § 609A.02, subd. 4 registration bar, treated as a hard bar here as a matter of policy.

tracks._componentsNote: An official participant-facing packet framework exists for this mechanism — EXP102 as the petition vehicle whose item 9 final checkbox routes to inherent authority, EXP104 as proof of service, and EXP107 as the published proposed order. It is deliberately NOT declared as official_pdf_fill components here, because the intake schema has no field for packet capability that is identified but not delivered: any official_pdf_fill component is normalized into a track-source relationship and a generation target, which would assert that LegalEase fills EXP107. Delivery is therefore recorded as process_guidance and packet identity is recorded in the component notes and the limitations, so that the record does not claim no packet exists.

components.notes: Explain the mechanism, explain that relief reaches judicial branch records only, and route the participant to legal aid or private counsel. Record, without generating: the official packet framework is EXP102 (petition vehicle; item 9's final checkbox routes to inherent authority), EXP104 (proof of service) and EXP107 (proposed order, Rev 01/15). Neutral participant identifier, case and service fields on EXP102 and EXP104 are mechanically completable. EXP107 is not: paragraphs 4, 5, 7 and 8 are findings against the petitioner, paragraphs 6, 8 and 9 are open-ended legal-argument fields including the clear-and-convincing balancing, and paragraphs 2 and 3 require case-specific conclusions of law.

tracks._limitationsNote: Every limitation is classified. Only legal_design_blocker withholds a track.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Packet identity and delivery scope are recorded separately. A participant-facing official packet framework exists: EXP102 is the petition vehicle and its item 9 final checkbox routes to inherent authority, EXP104 is proof of service, and EXP107 is the published proposed order. Direct self-help delivery is nonetheless outside current scope, and the reason is specific rather than a bare appeal to discretion. EXP107 is drafted as a court findings document: paragraphs 4, 5, 7 and 8 contain findings against the petitioner, paragraphs 6, 8 and 9 are open-ended legal-argument fields, and paragraphs 2 and 3 require case-specific conclusions of law. LegalEase cannot generate the constitutional-infringement analysis, cannot draft the balancing at paragraph 9, and cannot select among the conclusions of law without practising law. Those are the exact fields that prevent a completed self-help packet, and the proper output is a routed handoff to legal aid or private counsel. The intake schema was examined for a way to carry an attorney-handoff packet capability — neutral participant and case fields completable, legal-analysis fields left blank — and it has none: there is no packet-capability or delivery-scope field, and any component declared official_pdf_fill is normalized into a track-source relationship and an official-form generation target, which would assert that LegalEase fills EXP107. Delivery is therefore recorded as process_guidance with the packet framework preserved in the component notes and the limitations, rather than asserted as a generated packet.

limitations.statement: A participant-facing official packet framework exists — EXP102, EXP104 and EXP107 — but direct LegalEase delivery is outside current scope. Do not record this track as having no packet: packet identity is preserved and direct self-help filing is disabled.
